title: What to know before buying a rental property in Niagara
excerpt: An investor's checklist for analyzing rental properties in St. Catharines, Thorold, Welland and across Niagara.
content:
Niagara's mix of students, commuters and tourism and healthcare workers creates steady rental demand. But a good investment comes down to the numbers, not the listing photos.

Run the real numbers

Start with a realistic rent estimate based on comparable rentals, not optimistic projections. Then account for mortgage payments, property taxes, insurance, utilities you'll cover, maintenance, vacancy and property management if you won't self-manage.

Know your tenant pool

Properties near Brock University or Niagara College attract students; family homes in established neighbourhoods attract long-term tenants. Each has different management needs and risks.

Look for value-add potential

Homes with separate entrances, finished basements or zoning that allows additional units can boost income. Always confirm permits and zoning with the municipality.

Understand Ontario landlord rules

Ontario's Residential Tenancies Act sets the rules on leases, rent increases and ending tenancies. Learn them before you buy.
